title: Raising Kids Who Keep the Faith
subtitle: Forming a child's heart, not just their behavior — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the parent less worried about raising a well-behaved child than a child whose faith survives contact with the world.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Start with the uncomfortable truth that children learn faith from what you do, then move to the harder work of raising kids who can think and doubt out loud.

items.label: Your Kids Learn Faith From What You Do, Not What You Say
items.blurb: The catechism your children actually absorb is your ordinary Tuesday.

items.label: Raising Kids Who Think Instead of Just Performing Faith
items.blurb: A child who only performs belief has learned to hide, not to trust.

items.label: Teach Your Kids About Doubt Before the Internet Does
items.blurb: Someone will hand your child their hardest questions. Better that it is you.

items.label: When Your Child Asks a Question You Can't Answer
items.blurb: Saying you do not know is not the failure you fear. It may be the most honest discipleship you offer.

movements.heading: Then sit down at the table
movements.note: The Family Table is a guided study for discipling your own household — the meal, the text, the question, and the sending, scaled to a living room.

items.label: The Family Table — a study for households
items.blurb: A work-through study for making disciples of the children already at your table.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: Raising Kids in the Faith collects the work on handing down a faith worth keeping — prayer, the Bible at home, and family rhythms that hold. Free to read.

items.label: Raising Kids in the Faith — read free
items.blurb: Eleven chapters on forming faith at home. The complete book, free.

items.label: Find James's books in the bookstore
items.blurb: Print and ebook editions of the full library.
